title: A Ember for the Spire
premise: Edmund Marchetti has survived nine years as a royal food-taster by being poison-proof and perfectly forgettable, but a dying courier's map reveals he is the last living heir of Vessany, a kingdom erased from maps twenty years ago—and the usurper's inquisitors have finally traced the bloodline. Hunted through the Thornfell mountains alongside Sera, the courier's sharp-tongued daughter who blames him for her father's death, Edmund must follow the map to the Ember Gate, the only door out of a country that officially never existed. At the gate, Edmund learns the 'door' demands an heir's willing sacrifice of memory: to open it for thousands of refugees, he must forget Vessany, his heritage, and himself. He pays the price, and the free cities are saved by a man who will never know what he gave up—except that Sera stays behind to remember it for him.
about_author: Ada Galloway is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border treaties of defunct nations before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse near the mountains, where she keeps a drawer full of maps to countries that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In the usurper's palace, Edmund detects henbane in the king's stew and quietly saves a life no one thanks him for. We learn his craft, his careful invisibility, and the numbness beneath it. Emotional beat: competence as armor—the loneliness of a man whose only value is that he can die well.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A bleeding courier collapses in the palace kitchens' smuggling entrance, pressing a wax-sealed map into Edmund's hands and gasping a name: 'Vessany.' Guards approach; Edmund hides the stranger and the map both. Emotional beat: terror and a strange, unwelcome thrill—the first time anyone has chosen him for anything.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Deciphering the map in his garret, Edmund finds his own childhood home drawn at its heart, and a blood-seal that warms at his touch. The courier's words return: the heir must reach the Ember Gate. Emotional beat: vertigo—an identity he never asked for cracking open his carefully blank life.

chapters.title: Sera Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The courier's daughter ambushes Edmund in an alley, certain he stole her father's map and caused his death. She holds a knife; he offers the truth instead. Uneasy truce: she knows the mountains, he knows the seal. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into fury, then grudging alliance.

chapters.title: Nine Dishes of Poison
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Back at court, the taster-master grows suspicious of Edmund's absences; Edmund must swallow a suspect dish flawlessly while planning his flight. He poisons nothing but his own future, resigning in a way that cannot be traced. Emotional beat: the cost of leaving—the only safety he's ever known, burned behind him.

chapters.title: Into the Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The pair enters the mountains via smugglers' roads Sera grew up on. Cold, hunger, and her coldness toward Edmund. First glimpse of riders behind them—inquisitors in grey. Emotional beat: the wilderness strips away pretense; survival becomes the only honest language.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. They find a hidden settlement of Vessani survivors who recognize Edmund's face as the old royal line. An elder tells him how the kingdom was unmade—not conquered, but written out, its name forbidden. Emotional beat: belonging offered like a wound; Edmund realizes people have been waiting for him.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Grey Riders burn the village two days after they leave. Sera drags survivors into the high passes and, watching Edmund risk everything for strangers, stops hating him. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted—she couldn't save her father, but she can save these.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Question
chapters.summary: POV antagonist, Inquisitor Corvane. Corvane interrogates the captured taster-master and reconstructs Edmund's escape. Flashbacks reveal the purge of Vessany was Corvane's first commission. Emotional beat: chilling patience—a hunter who believes erasure is mercy.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Gospel
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A smuggler caravan agrees to move refugees for a price: the map itself. Edmund refuses; Sera secretly negotiates a copy. Their first real fight—and first real honesty about her father's death. Emotional beat: trust forged in conflict, not comfort.

chapters.title: The Pass of Names
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Crossing a pass where Vessani tradition says the dead speak, Sera confesses her father died carrying the map to Edmund deliberately—he believed the heir would finish what he started. Edmund absorbs that he was someone's hope. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither of them asks for aloud.

chapters.title: Grey Riders at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Ambush at a river crossing. Edmund uses his poisoner's knowledge—doctoring the Riders' water canteens—to buy the refugees time, nearly dying of his own concoction. Emotional beat: his curse-turned-craft; the taster finally tastes his own medicine.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. Cornering Edmund alone, Corvane offers legitimacy: renounce Vessany publicly and live rich and safe in the usurper's court. He shows Edmund records proving his parents betrayed the kingdom first. Emotional beat: seduction of despair—the lie that surrender is wisdom.

chapters.title: What My Parents Did
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Shaken, Edmund examines the records with Sera and finds them doctored—his parents died sealing the map's route, not selling it. He refuses Corvane's offer and the inquisitor marks every refugee for death. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; he chooses the burden over the bargain.

chapters.title: Winter Camp
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Snowbound with the refugee column, small human moments: songs in the forbidden tongue, children born on the road, Edmund teaching Sera to read the old script. Quiet before the storm. Emotional beat: love arriving without announcement, in shared bread and borrowed warmth.

chapters.title: The Ember Gate Found
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following the map's final riddle, they find the Gate: a door in a cliff face that opens onto nowhere, guarded by a blind warden who tests Edmund's blood and names the price—to open it wide enough for all, an heir must feed it their memory of Vessany, forever. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Warden's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The Gate can open narrowly for one, or fully for many—at the cost of the heir's entire inheritance of self. Sera argues for alternatives; there are none. Edmund decides before dawn, asking only that someone remember for him. Emotional beat: grief in advance, mourning a man still breathing.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: POV multiple. Corvane's army crests the ridge above the refugee camp as the Gate begins to wake. Battle in the snow; Sera holds the pass with smugglers and villagers against impossible odds. Emotional beat: desperate courage—every life bought minute by minute.

chapters.title: An Ember for the Spire
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the Gate, Edmund feeds it his memories one by one—his mother's kitchen, the palace kitchens, Sera's face in firelight—until nothing of Vessany or himself remains. The Gate blazes open. Emotional beat: transcendence through erasure; the title's meaning revealed—the last ember spent to light the way out.

chapters.title: Through
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Refugees pour through as Corvane breaks the pass. Sera finds Edmund standing blank-eyed before the open door, not knowing her. She walks him through last as the Gate seals, cutting off Corvane forever. Emotional beat: victory and bereavement entwined—she saved him and lost him in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Free Cities
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In the free cities, the refugees begin new lives under a name no law can erase: the ones who came through. Sera takes work keeping the old records alive. Edmund, a stranger to himself, is drawn to her archive without knowing why. Emotional beat: fragile hope—identity rebuilt from kindness rather than blood.

chapters.title: Remember Me
chapters.summary: POV Sera, closing letter to Edmund. Sera begins telling him their story, one evening at a time, keeping her promise to remember for both of them. The final image: two cups of tea, an open book of maps, and a man learning to be someone new. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love as the archive that survives erasure.
